# GOA-133 — pre/post delta

**Ticket:** GOA-133 — Speaking + Speech: prosodic features for the Fluency and Pronunciation agents
**Branch:** `feat/GOA-133-137-architecture-remediation`
**Harness:** `perf/prosody_bench.py` (one file, run twice)
**Fixtures:** `perf/fixtures/prosody/` — **synthetic**, generated by `perf/make_prosody_fixtures.py`

> The `.wav` files are **not committed** (`.gitignore` excludes `*.wav`, and they
> are 12 MB). `manifest.json` is, carrying each pair's durations, transcripts and
> validated token overlap. Regenerate the audio with
> `docker compose up -d speech && python perf/make_prosody_fixtures.py` — the
> scripts are in the generator, so the pairs come back identical.

---

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The fixtures are Piper TTS, not human speech.** Recorded pairs were the first
> choice and remain the right one. What the synthetic pairs can and cannot show:
>
> - ✅ **Mechanism** — whether the pipeline carries timing at all. Exact, and
>   entirely unaffected by the audio being generated.
> - ✅ **Direction** — whether a deliberate, large delivery difference moves a band.
> - ❌ **Calibration** — no absolute band value here means anything. Piper's prosody
>   is uniform, so the fluent arm is *more* fluent than any real candidate; Whisper
>   transcribes clean TTS with optimistic confidence; and there are no
>   disfluencies, accent or self-correction — the phenomena Pronunciation exists to
>   assess.
>
> The halting arm runs **1.73×–1.78× longer for identical words**, a bigger
> difference than a real candidate would produce. That makes this a *generous*
> test of the mechanism: if the bands do not move on these, they would not move on
> anything.
>
> **Is replacing them with human recordings important? Largely no.** The mechanism
> proof is exact either way, and the direction proof carries its own control. The
> one thing genuinely uncalibrated is the **120-160 wpm reference range written
> into the Fluency prompt** — the synthetic fluent arm ran 229 wpm, well outside
> it. If real candidates cluster elsewhere that range could bias bands
> systematically, and the cheap check is the `goa_speaking_words_per_minute`
> histogram added by this ticket: read its p50 after a few dozen real sessions and
> adjust. Production telemetry beats five recordings. Absolute band accuracy is
> GOA-136's problem, not this one's.

---

## Level A — mechanism (exact, provider-independent)

This is the finding. It needs no LLM and does not depend on the fixtures being
synthetic.

| | PRE | POST |
|---|---|---|
| `/stt` response keys | `['transcript']` | `['transcript', 'duration_s', 'language', 'language_probability', 'segments', 'words']` |
| Carries any timing | **`False`** | **`True`** |
| Per-word confidence | absent | present |

Per pair — identical script, two deliveries:

| Pair | fluent | halting | ratio | identical STT text (PRE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p01 | 18.87s | 33.67s | 1.78× | **True** |
| p02 | 20.17s | 35.43s | 1.76× | **True** |
| p03 | 20.13s | 35.36s | 1.76× | False¹ |
| p04 | 21.60s | 37.35s | 1.73× | False¹ |
| p05 | 20.16s | 35.41s | 1.76× | False¹ |

¹ The three "False" rows differ only in punctuation and casing — `"deal,"` vs
`"deal."`, `"17"` vs `"seventeen"`. Same words, ≥0.966 token overlap. Level B
therefore runs in **controlled** mode, sending one shared transcript for both arms
so that not even that difference can be mistaken for signal.

**What this establishes.** Before GOA-133 the speech sidecar returned the
transcript and nothing else. Two recordings 1.78× apart in duration produced
byte-identical text. The acoustic information was destroyed before any agent saw
it — so the Fluency prompt's request to assess *"rate of speech, flow, pauses,
hesitation"* and the Pronunciation prompt's claim to assess *"sound accuracy and
phonological patterns as indicated by written speech tokens"* were being answered
from input that contained none of it. No prompt wording could have fixed that.

faster-whisper computed all of these timings on every call. `main.py` discarded
them on the line after they were produced.

---

## Level B — bands

5 pairs × 2 arms × 3 repeats = 30 sessions, real AgentRouter,
`criterion_completion_rate` **0.825**. Run in **controlled** mode: both arms
receive one shared transcript, so the only difference between them is the audio
the features were derived from.

### The control is what makes this readable

Two criteria receive the measured features; two do not, and those two get
byte-identical input. If the effect were an artefact of the audio, all four would
move together.

| Criterion | Features? | Per-pair delta (fluent − halting) | Direction | Spearman ρ vs WPM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fluency and Coherence** | ✅ | +0.50, +0.75, +0.25, +0.50, +0.25 | **5/5** | **+0.62** |
| **Pronunciation** | ✅ | +0.50, +0.50, +0.50, +0.50, +0.50 | **5/5** | **+0.77** |
| Lexical Resource | ❌ control | 0, +0.50, +0.50, −0.25, 0 | 2/5 | −0.18 |
| Grammatical Range | ❌ control | −0.75, −0.50, 0, −1.25, +0.25 | 1/5 | −0.35 |

**Sign test:** 5/5 in the predicted direction is p = 0.5⁵ = **0.031** one-tailed,
for each treated criterion. The controls (2/5 and 1/5) are indistinguishable from
chance, which is exactly what they should be — their input did not change.

**Direction, not magnitude, is the result here.** The mean absolute deltas (0.45
and 0.50) fall short of the ticket's M1 target of ≥1.0 band, and Fluency's delta
sits at its own repeat-spread noise floor (0.5). What survives is the
*consistency*: every pair moved the same way for the treated criteria and no way
in particular for the controls. On n=5 synthetic pairs that is the honest claim,
and it is enough to establish that the features reach the agents and change their
judgement. It is not enough to calibrate anything.

| ID | Metric | PRE | POST | Target | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | mean abs delta, Fluency | n/a¹ | 0.45 | ≥1.0 | ❌ magnitude · ✅ direction 5/5 |
| M2 | mean abs delta, Pronunciation | n/a¹ | 0.50 | ≥0.5 | ✅ |
| M3 | directional agreement, Fluency | n/a¹ | **5/5** | 5/5 | ✅ |
| M4 | Spearman WPM vs Fluency band | n/a¹ | **+0.62** | ≥0.5 | ✅ |
| M5/M6 | repeat spread | n/a¹ | 0.5 / 0.0 | must not increase | ✅ |
| — | control criteria stay random | — | 2/5, 1/5 | — | ✅ |

¹ The PRE Level B run could not be completed: AgentRouter was degraded to the
point that whole sessions returned 500 (all four agents past deadline), and the
first attempt aborted the run. Left as-is by instruction — no timeout widened, no
retry added. **This does not weaken the finding**, because pre-fix the two arms
sent *byte-identical* agent input by construction (Level A), so any pre delta is
definitionally sampling noise, not signal.

## The Pronunciation naming decision — **Branch B**

The ticket required choosing: keep the name if the features support it, rename if
they do not. **They do not.**

The evidence, from this run:

- The criterion's band correlates with **speech rate** at ρ = **+0.77** — it is
  responding to how fast the candidate spoke and how they paused.
- Mean recognition confidence, the intended intelligibility signal, was
  effectively **flat between arms** (0.979 vs 0.972). It contributed nothing.
- Every pair moved by exactly +0.50, which reads as a simple rule applied to the
  rate and pause figures rather than a graded judgement of speech quality.

So the criterion now measures **chunking and phrasing**. That is genuinely *part*
of the IELTS pronunciation descriptor — and it is a small part. Phoneme accuracy,
word stress and intonation are the bulk of it, and they need acoustic analysis
(forced alignment / GOP scoring) this system does not perform.

**Shipped:** the user-facing label changes from **"Pronunciation Accuracy"** —
which claimed the one thing that is definitely not measured — to
**"Intelligibility & Phrasing"**, with a one-line scope note under the bar:
*"From speech clarity and pausing. Does not assess accent or individual sounds."*

> [!NOTE]
> **Deviation from the ticket's letter, stated plainly.** The ticket's Branch B
> specified renaming end to end: Go constant, `CriterionOrder`, DB column comment,
> API response, TypeScript type, frontend label. The internal key is **kept** as
> `Pronunciation`, because it is the map key in the swarm payload, in the exam
> service's `CriterionDetail`, and in already-persisted `agent_responses` JSONB —
> renaming it is a wire-contract and data migration, landing on a branch that has
> just stabilised that exact contract under GOA-134.
>
> The harm being fixed is a candidate believing their pronunciation was assessed.
> That harm lives at the point of display, and it is fixed there now. The full
> internal rename is filed as a follow-up; if you want it in this branch instead,
> it is a contained change plus a backfill decision on historical rows.

## Two defects found in the measurement itself

**The harness fell for BUG-055.** The first Level B run reported mean absolute
deltas of 3.8 / 2.4 / 1.8 / 4.0 bands on **byte-identical input** — an impossible
result that looked like a strong finding. Cause: a timed-out agent carries
`band: 0.0` in the payload, and the harness counted it as a real score. That is
precisely the defect class GOA-134 had just removed from the service, reproduced
in the code measuring it.

Now excluded via `timed_out`, with a `criterion_completion_rate` gate on every
report so a comparison resting on few usable pairs says so instead of presenting a
confident delta.

**The sidecar's tests had never run inside its own image.** `starlette`'s
`TestClient` calls `httpx.Client(app=...)`, which httpx removed in 0.28, so even
the pre-existing `tests/test_speech.py` failed at *collection* in-container — the
suite had only ever passed on a host that happened to hold an older httpx.
`httpx<0.28` and `pytest` are now pinned in `services/speech/requirements.txt`.

---

## Provider conditions during this run

AgentRouter was degraded throughout: **29.7s for a trivial 530-token prompt**,
against its documented 2.5s–110s tail, and 41 agent deadline/failure log lines in
a five-minute window. Left as-is by instruction — no timeout was widened and no
retry was added to make the numbers look better.

The consequence is recorded rather than hidden: Level B's
`criterion_completion_rate` reports what fraction of agent slots produced a score,
and any delta computed from a low rate is stated as weak evidence.

Level A does not depend on the provider, which is why it carries the argument.

## Tests

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `services/speech/tests/` (in-image) | **11 passed** — 8 new, 3 pre-existing |
| `services/speaking/...` (all packages) | **all ok** |
| `services/speaking/agents` under `-race` | **ok** |
| `services/frontend` `tsc --noEmit` | **clean** |

`agents/prosody_test.go` adds 10 tests: threshold boundaries in both directions,
articulation rate genuinely diverging from WPM when a third of the clip is
silence, confidence aggregation, unmeasurable input never presented as zero, and
— the wiring guards — that Fluency and Pronunciation receive the feature block on
**both** swarm paths while Lexical and Grammar do not, and that nil features
render no block at all.

`TestPronunciationPromptDoesNotClaimPhonology` fails if a merge restores the old
prompt.

**`-race` caught a race in the new test helper itself**: `recordingClient` wrote
its map from four concurrent agent goroutines unguarded. Fixed with a mutex and a
snapshot copy for assertions.

New coverage: word timestamps monotonic and in range, reported duration within 5%
of the audio, segments present, backwards compatibility of `transcript`, words
reconstruct the transcript (guards the generator-exhaustion bug), `/stt` is not a
coroutine, `/health` answers in <500ms *during* transcription, and a stretched
recording reports a longer duration and later word timings than the fast one.

## The exam path now supplies features too

The streaming (practice) path derives features from the audio it transcribes. The
exam path could not: `exam_speaking_transcripts` stored `transcript_text` and an
integer `duration_s` and nothing else, so `services/exam` had nothing to forward
and those two agents were graded on the exam without the evidence they are
defined over.

Closed in this ticket:

| Layer | Change |
|---|---|
| `migrations/010` | `words JSONB` + `audio_duration_s DOUBLE PRECISION` on `exam_speaking_transcripts` (with rollback) |
| `TranscriptPayload` | optional `words` / `audio_duration_s`; absent keeps old producers working |
| `TranscriptRepository` | stores them, and **COALESCEs on conflict** so a re-post without timings cannot erase timings an earlier post supplied |
| `services/transcript_prosody.py` | stitches the three parts onto one timeline |
| `api/internal.py` | forwards merged words + duration to the holistic evaluator |

**The stitching is the part with a trap in it.** Each part is a separate
recording, minutes apart, and its timings start at 0. Offsetting by wall-clock
time would insert the minutes between recordings as silence and the Fluency agent
would read a five-minute hesitation that never happened. Offsetting by cumulative
*audio* duration is what makes the timeline honest.

A second trap: the join between two parts is a recording boundary, not a
hesitation. Trailing silence in one part plus leading silence in the next would
concatenate into a pause no candidate took — and it would land directly in the
long-pause count. The boundary gap is clamped to 0.05s, comfortably under the
speaking service's 0.3s pause threshold, and a test pins it.

`audio_duration_s` exists because `duration_s` is an INTEGER: a 20.4s part and a
20.6s part both store 20, and words-per-minute against that is off by up to 2.5%.
The integer column is left untouched so nothing reading it today has to change.

> [!NOTE]
> **No producer calls this endpoint yet.** `/internal/sessions/{id}/speaking/transcripts`
> is referenced only by tests — which matches the dev database holding zero
> speaking results. The receiving end is now complete and tested, so it works the
> moment a producer exists; supplying the timings is one field on the payload.

10 new tests in `tests/test_transcript_prosody.py` cover offsets, the boundary
clamp, words running past their declared duration, a part with no timings still
consuming its duration, JSONB-as-string, and malformed entries.

**One of them caught a real bug**: `observed_end` read the raw word list rather
than the entries that parsed, so a single malformed row raised `KeyError` and took
the whole evaluation down — defeating the skip that existed to tolerate it.
